agent_note: The stage agent named by SARVAM_AGENT_ID in .env (Tiffany Designs Customer Service Stage). The earlier agent Tiffany-Des-0db8e21d-e099 still exists, with its own older tools calling https://tiffany-designs-customer-service.onrender.com/.
draft_note: Version 14 (committed 2026-10-29) has every tool below as written here and the prompt in agent-prompt.md. identify_caller runs at call start (lifecycle on_start): it sends Sarvam's caller identifier to /api/agent/call-start and saves customer_phone, customer_name, opening_line and caller_details, so a phone caller is greeted by name and never asked for the mobile number. get_product_guide with purpose assembly gives the complete product guide, every numbered step with its own hardware, and step_count; when a found guide has no steps (or the server has not been deployed with this yet) its answer says so and the agent offers an installation visit instead of making steps up. Until the server is deployed, call-start fails harmlessly and the call goes on as before. The live deployment answers with the version it names; move it to 14 to use this. Draft 15 is an unchanged copy.
base_url_note: The server is deployed on Render. Every tool calls current_base_url + path with POST and a JSON body; change all of them together if the server moves.
response_note: Every tool answers HTTP 200 with a flat JSON object, refusals and failures included. What the agent hears is resp_template (Send fields from the API response to the agent): the message, then a Fields line with the fields in send_to_agent, for example Fields: found=True, order_id=TD-ORD-1001, open_requests=['installation']. A field the answer lacks renders empty, and error appears only when the service system did not answer. on_failure is what the agent hears when the call itself fails (timeout or a non-200). save_to_variables maps agent variables to response fields; the call-end webhook reads case_number and placed_order_number.

common_response_fields.message: What to tell the customer, plus instructions for the agent such as what to ask next. Never read out word for word.
common_response_fields.error: unavailable when the service system did not answer; absent otherwise.

tools.name: identify_caller
tools.description: Runs when the call starts, before the greeting. Sends the number the customer is calling from to the service system, which puts it in customer_phone, looks it up, and fills caller_details with what is on record for it (name, recent orders, open requests, or not on record). When the number belongs to a customer it also sets customer_name to the first name and opening_line to a greeting by name. Outbound and website calls keep the values they already have.

response_fields.customer_phone: The number of the call, E.164: the website number when one was typed, else the phone caller's number; saved to customer_phone.
response_fields.customer_name: The first name of the customer the number belongs to, or the name already set; saved to customer_name.
response_fields.opening_line: The greeting by first name for a known caller, else the greeting already set; saved to opening_line.
response_fields.caller_details: What is on record for the number (name, recent orders, open requests) or that it is not on record; saved to caller_details.
response_fields.known_customer: true when the number belongs to a customer.

tools.name: find_customer
tools.description: Finds the customer by mobile number or, when the customer does not know the registered mobile, by full name and the six digit PIN code of their address. On an inbound call where customer_phone is set, call it with that number before the first reply, without asking. The answer has a message with the customer's name, recent orders and open requests, and the fields found, first_name (the name to address the customer by), customer_name, latest_order_id and open_requests (how many requests are open). When nothing is found, carry on without saying so.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's mobile number: the value of customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the 10 digit number the customer gave. Leave empty when the customer does not know it.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's full name, first and last, when searching without the mobile number.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: The six digit PIN code of the customer's address, when searching without the mobile number.

response_fields.found: true when exactly one customer matches.
response_fields.first_name: First name to address the customer by.
response_fields.recent_orders: Recent order ids with their delivery status.
response_fields.latest_order_id: The newest order id, or null.
response_fields.open_requests: How many service requests are open.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, first_name={{ first_name | default('') }}, customer_name={{ customer_name | default('') }}, latest_order_id={{ latest_order_id | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The customer lookup did not answer. Call tool:find_customer once more. When it fails again, carry on without the customer record and without saying so, and ask for the order id, order number or invoice number when the concern needs an order.

tools.name: find_order
tools.description: Finds an order and gives its products, delivery status and delivery date, the kinds of request already open on it, and whether the order has the customer's mobile number and a delivery address on record. Call it as soon as the customer gives any one of: the order id (for example TD-ORD-1001, ORD-010, or only the number at its end such as 1001), the order number of a phone order (digits, for example 122), or the invoice number (for example INV-2001, or only its digits). No mobile number or name is needed. With only a mobile number it gives the latest order on that number. The answer has a message with the facts and what to do next, and the fields found, order_id, order_number, delivery_status, products, open_requests (installation, installation_followup, damage or replacement), mobile_on_order, address_on_order and details_missing. When no order is found after a second try, or details_missing is true, offer the WhatsApp invoice upload link with tool:send_invoice_upload_link.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id as the customer said it, written without spaces, for example TD-ORD-1001 or ORD-010. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: An order number of digits only, for example 122 or 00000122, when the customer gives digits instead of an order id. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: The invoice number as the customer said it, written without spaces, for example INV-2001. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit mobile number when it is already known: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the number the customer gave. Leave empty when not known; it is not needed to find an order by its number.

response_fields.order_id: The order id, or null for a phone order.
response_fields.customer_name: Account name on the order. Not sent to the agent, so a name is never confirmed from an order id.
response_fields.delivery_status: Delivered, Shipped, Processing and so on.
response_fields.delivery_date: Delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD; the message says it as weekday and date.
response_fields.open_requests: Kinds of request open on the order: installation, installation_followup, damage, replacement.
response_fields.mobile_on_order: true when the order's customer has a mobile number on record.
response_fields.address_on_order: true when the order has a delivery address to visit: a street, and a city or PIN code.
response_fields.details_missing: true when either is missing; the agent then offers the WhatsApp invoice upload link (Phase 15).

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, order_id={{ order_id | default('') }}, order_number={{ order_number | default('') }}, delivery_status={{ delivery_status | default('') }}, products={{ products | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if details_missing is defined %}, mobile_on_order={{ mobile_on_order }}, address_on_order={{ address_on_order }}, details_missing={{ details_missing }}{% endif %}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The order lookup did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:find_order once more. When it fails again, note the order id as the customer gave it and carry on without the order.

tools.name: get_details_on_file
tools.description: Gets the mobile number and address on file for an order (its customer and delivery address) or for a registered mobile number, so they are confirmed with the customer instead of asked for again. Call it before registering a service request, a return, a replacement or a call back, once the order was found or the registered mobile is known, without asking first. Only the last four digits of the mobile and the city, state and PIN code are given; the request tools fill in the rest with use_details_on_file. The answer has a message saying what is on file and what to ask for, and the fields found, mobile_on_file, mobile_ending, address_on_file, city and postal_code.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id that found the order, written without spaces, for example TD-ORD-1001 or ORD-010. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: The order number of digits that found the order, for example 122. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: The invoice number that found the order, for example INV-2001. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's registered 10 digit mobile number when no order is known: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the number the customer gave. Leave empty when an order reference is given.

response_fields.found: true when an order or customer was found.
response_fields.mobile_on_file: true when a mobile number is on file.
response_fields.mobile_ending: Last four digits of that mobile.
response_fields.address_on_file: true when a city or PIN code is on file.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, mobile_on_file={{ mobile_on_file | default('') }}, mobile_ending={{ mobile_ending | default('') }}, address_on_file={{ address_on_file | default('') }}, city={{ city | default('') }}, postal_code={{ postal_code | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The details on file did not answer. Ask the customer for the 10 digit mobile number, then the house, street and area, the city and the six digit PIN code, one at a time.

tools.name: get_installation_address
tools.description: For an installation, gives the city, state and PIN code of the address the order was delivered to, or of the customer's address on file when the order has none, and the last four digits of the mobile number on file. Call it once the order is found, without asking first, then ask whether the installation should be at that address or somewhere else. When the customer chooses it, book_installation is called with at_delivery_address set to true and the service system fills in the full address. The street and the full mobile number are never given. The answer has a message to say back and what to ask next, and the fields found, address_source (delivery, customer, or empty when no address is on record), city, postal_code, mobile_on_file and mobile_ending.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id that found the order, written without spaces, for example TD-ORD-1001 or ORD-010. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: The order number of digits that found the order, for example 122. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: The invoice number that found the order, for example INV-2001. Leave empty when not known.

response_fields.found: true when the order was found.
response_fields.delivered: true when the order is delivered.
response_fields.address_source: delivery, customer, or null when no address is on record.
response_fields.mobile_on_file: true when a mobile number is on file.
response_fields.mobile_ending: Last four digits of that mobile.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, address_source={{ address_source | default('') }}, city={{ city | default('') }}, postal_code={{ postal_code | default('') }}, mobile_on_file={{ mobile_on_file | default('') }}, mobile_ending={{ mobile_ending | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The installation address did not answer. Ask where the installation should be: the house, street and area, then the city, then the six digit PIN code, one at a time.

tools.name: send_invoice_upload_link
tools.description: Sends the customer a WhatsApp link to upload a photo, a screenshot or a PDF of the invoice. Use it when the order cannot be found, or when tool:find_order says the order has no mobile number or no delivery address on record. The service system reads the invoice, finds the order by its invoice number, order id or mobile number, and completes the order with the details on the invoice; the customer then calls again to have the concern resolved. Call it only after the customer agreed to get the link and the WhatsApp number was confirmed. At most 3 links per number a day. The answer has a message saying what to tell the customer, or why no link was sent, and the field sent.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit WhatsApp number as confirmed with the customer: customer_phone or the mobile number given earlier in the call when the customer said it is on WhatsApp, otherwise the number the customer gave for WhatsApp.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's name: customer_name when it is set, otherwise the name the customer gave. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: order_reference
parameters.description: The order id, order number or invoice number that found the order, or that the customer gave on this call even though no order was found for it, written without spaces. Leave empty when none was given.

response_fields.sent: true when the link was sent.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: sent={{ sent | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The WhatsApp link could not be sent right now. Carry on with the concern without it: note the order id, invoice number and product as the customer gives them, and ask for any missing mobile number or address.

tools.name: get_product_guide
tools.description: Gets the product guide for the products on an order, or for a product the customer names. By default (purpose parts) it says what comes in the set and gives every part with its sticker number, quantity and part number, the hardware by letter, the delivery check groups, and the rules for that product, such as safety advice. Use it for a damaged, defective, missing or wrong part: ask about one part at a time, how many the set should have and how many arrived, and pass the right part number. With purpose assembly it gives the complete product guide: what the product is, its size and material, what comes in the set, the tools needed, the parts by sticker number, the hardware by letter, a parts check before starting, every assembly step numbered in order with the hardware that step uses, the tips, safety and care advice, the rules and the warranty. Review the whole guide and use it to guide a customer who assembles the product alone, one step at a time, giving nothing the guide does not have. The answer has a message with the guide and the fields found, has_assembly_steps and, for assembly, step_count; when found is false, use tool:find_parts for parts, or offer an installation visit for assembly.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id that found the order, written without spaces, for example TD-ORD-1001 or ORD-010. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: order_number
parameters.description: The order number of digits that found the order, for example 122. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: The invoice number that found the order, for example INV-2001. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product the customer named, in English, for example kitchen island or wardrobe, when no order is known. Leave empty when an order reference is given.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit mobile number when it is already known: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the number the customer gave. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: parts for a damaged, defective, missing or wrong part, which is the default; assembly when the customer wants to assemble the product alone or needs help with an assembly step.

response_fields.found: true when a published guide exists.
response_fields.purpose: parts (the default) or assembly, as the guide was asked for.
response_fields.has_assembly_steps: true when the guide has assembly steps to walk the customer through.
response_fields.products: Each product with parts_have_number_stickers and its parts (name, part_number).
response_fields.step_count: With purpose assembly, how many numbered assembly steps the guide has; 0 when it has none. Absent for parts.

tools.on_failure: The product guide did not answer. For a part, match it with tool:find_parts instead. For assembly help, offer an installation visit by the service team.

tools.name: find_parts
tools.description: Lists the parts of the products on an order, or of a product the customer names, with their part numbers. Use it when tool:get_product_guide has no guide, to match the damaged, defective, missing or wrong part and pass its part number when registering the request. The answer has a message listing each part with its part number, and the field found.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The verified order id, for example TD-ORD-1001. Leave empty when the order is not known.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product the customer named, for example wardrobe or study table. Used when the order id is not known.

response_fields.found: true when parts are on record.
response_fields.parts: Each part with name, part_number and product.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The part list did not answer. Record the part as the customer describes it and carry on.

tools.name: resolve_date
tools.description: Checks the installation day, and the time when one is given, using today's date and the time now in India. Installation visits are Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and only for a day and time still ahead; a Sunday, a time outside those hours or a time already passed is refused with what to ask instead. Call it with the day the customer said, then again with that date and the time the customer said, before reading the slot back. Never work out a date or time without it. The answer has a message to read back, and the fields valid, date (YYYY-MM-DD, for book_installation as preferred_date), spoken_date (weekday and date to say) and time (for book_installation as preferred_time).

parameters.name: date_text
parameters.description: The installation day or date the customer said, in English, for example today, tomorrow, day after tomorrow, Saturday, next Monday, 17 October or 17/10, or the YYYY-MM-DD date from an earlier resolve_date answer.

parameters.name: time_text
parameters.description: The installation time the customer said, written in English as a clock time with am or pm, for example 11 am, 3 pm, 2 pm to 4 pm or after 3 pm, or as morning, afternoon or evening when the customer gave only that. Leave empty when only the day is being checked.

response_fields.valid: true when the day, and the time when given, can be used.
response_fields.date: The date as YYYY-MM-DD, to pass to book_installation as preferred_date.
response_fields.spoken_date: The date as weekday and date, to say back.
response_fields.time: The checked time, for example 11 am or morning, 10 am to 12 pm, to pass to book_installation as preferred_time; null without time_text.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: valid={{ valid | default('') }}, date={{ date | default('') }}, spoken_date={{ spoken_date | default('') }}, time={{ time | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The date check did not answer. Ask for the day and month, then call tool:resolve_date once more. When it fails again, pass the day and the time as the customer said them to tool:book_installation, which checks them itself.

tools.name: book_installation
tools.description: Registers an installation request, or a request to move one, with the customer's preferred slot. The slot must be Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm, and still ahead; it is checked again and nothing is registered when it does not fit. Pass the date and the time from the latest resolve_date answer, after the customer confirmed the slot and the place. The service team confirms the final appointment. When the customer chose the address from get_installation_address, set at_delivery_address to true and leave the address empty; when the customer agreed to the mobile number on file, set use_details_on_file to true and leave the mobile empty. A second installation request on an order that has one open needs new_request set to true. The answer has a message with the request number and slot to give, or what to ask instead, and the fields created, spoken_case_number (say it digit by digit), existing_request (true when one is already open and nothing was registered) and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: preferred_date
parameters.description: The installation date from the latest resolve_date answer, in YYYY-MM-DD form.

parameters.name: preferred_time
parameters.description: The installation time from the latest resolve_date answer, for example 11 am, 2 pm to 4 pm, or morning, 10 am to 12 pm.

parameters.name: reschedule
parameters.description: True when the customer wants to move an installation that was already requested.

parameters.name: existing_case_number
parameters.description: The earlier installation request number, for a reschedule, when the customer has it.

parameters.name: at_delivery_address
parameters.description: True when the customer chose to have the installation at the address from get_installation_address. The service system then fills in that full address, so address, city and PIN code are left empty.

parameters.name: use_details_on_file
parameters.description: True when the customer agreed to use the mobile number on file. The service system then fills it in.

parameters.name: new_request
parameters.description: True only when an installation request is already open on the order and the customer said a new request is wanted.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit mobile number: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the number the customer gave. Leave empty when use_details_on_file is true.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's full name.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id or order number that found the order, when known.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: The invoice number, when known.

parameters.name: order_source
parameters.description: Where the order was bought, when no order was found and the customer said so.

parameters.name: product_name
parameters.description: The product to install.

parameters.name: address

parameters.name: city

parameters.name: postal_code

parameters.name: state

response_fields.created: true when the request is registered.
response_fields.spoken_case_number: The request number to say, digit by digit, for example 1100.
response_fields.existing_request: true when an installation request is already open on the order and nothing was registered.
response_fields.within_business_hours: false when registered outside service hours.
response_fields.order_verified: true when the request is linked to the order.

tools.name: register_service_request
tools.description: Registers a service request for a damaged, defective, missing or wrong part, a product quality problem, a replacement, a return, an installation follow-up, a re-installation or a general question. Salesforce routes it to the Delhi NCR service team or a service partner from the city and PIN code. Call it once, after the customer confirmed the summary. When the customer agreed to the mobile number and address from get_details_on_file, set use_details_on_file to true and leave them empty; pass only details the customer changed. A second request of the same kind on an order that has one open needs new_request set to true. The answer has a message with the request number to give, or what is missing, and the fields created, spoken_case_number (say it digit by digit), existing_request (true when one of this kind is already open and nothing was registered) and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: issue_type
parameters.description: The kind of request: damaged for a part damaged after delivery, delivery_damage for damage found when the package was opened, defective for a part that does not work properly, missing_parts, wrong_part, quality_issue, replacement, return, installation_followup for a problem after installation, reinstallation, or general for any other question.

tools.name: request_human_callback
tools.description: Registers a request for a member of the service team to call the customer back. Use it when the customer asks for a person, stays upset, reports an injury or a safety risk, says a delivered order never arrived, asks to be called at a later time, or when the agent cannot help. No live transfer is available. When the customer agreed to the mobile number and address from get_details_on_file, set use_details_on_file to true and leave the mobile number, city and PIN code empty. The answer has a message with the request number to give, and the fields created, spoken_case_number (say it digit by digit) and within_business_hours.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why a person needs to call back, in one plain English sentence, including any time the customer asked to be called and any other number they gave.

parameters.name: use_details_on_file
parameters.description: True when the customer agreed to use the mobile number and address on file from get_details_on_file.

parameters.name: phone

parameters.name: order_id

{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_case_number={{ spoken_case_number | default('') }}, within_business_hours={{ within_business_hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The call back request could not be registered because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:request_human_callback once more with the same details. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will call back during service hours.

tools.name: check_request_status
tools.description: Gives the status of the customer's open service requests, with any scheduled technician visit and replacement part shipment. With the registered mobile number it gives that customer's open requests. Without the mobile, it needs the request number plus the full name on the request or the order id it is about. The answer has a message with the status to give, and the fields found, status (of the newest request) and open_requests (how many the answer covers).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's mobile number: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the 10 digit number the customer gave. Leave empty when the customer does not know it.

parameters.name: case_number
parameters.description: The service request number the customer gave, digits only. Leave empty to list all open requests on the mobile number.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's full name, first and last, when the mobile number is not known.

parameters.name: order_id
parameters.description: The order id the request is about, for example TD-ORD-1001, when the mobile number is not known.

response_fields.found: true when a matching request was found.
response_fields.case_number: Salesforce number of the newest request; the message has it as spoken.
response_fields.open_requests: How many requests the answer covers.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, status={{ status | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The request status did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:check_request_status once more. When it fails again, offer a call back from the service team.

tools.name: get_service_history
tools.description: Lists the customer's latest service requests, closed ones included, and their latest calls with Tiffany Designs, by the registered mobile number. Use it when the customer asks about earlier calls or past requests. The answer has a message with the history, most recent first, and the fields found and open_requests (how many are still open).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's mobile number: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the 10 digit number the customer gave.

response_fields.found: true when any request or call is on record.
response_fields.open_requests: How many of those requests are still open.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}, open_requests={{ open_requests | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service history did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:get_service_history once more. When it fails again, offer a call back from the service team.

tools.name: check_service_hours
tools.description: Says whether the Tiffany Designs service team is working right now and until when, or when it opens again, from the service hours and holidays in Salesforce, with the weekly hours. Use it when the customer asks about timings or wants to speak to a person, and before saying when the team will call back. The answer has a message to give, and the fields open (true when the team is working now) and hours (the weekly hours in words).

response_fields.open: true when the team is working now.
response_fields.closes_at: When it closes today, as a timestamp.
response_fields.next_open: When it opens again, as a timestamp.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: open={{ open | default('') }}, hours={{ hours | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service hours did not answer. Say the service team works Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 6 pm, and carry on.

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Says who handles service visits at a location: the Tiffany Designs service team in Delhi NCR, or an authorised service partner elsewhere, by the same rules Salesforce routes requests with. Also checks that the PIN code is valid. Use it after settling the city and PIN code for a request that needs a visit. The answer has a message to give, and the fields valid (false when the PIN code is not valid) and route (Internal or External Provider).

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: The city the customer gave, for example Gurugram or Jaipur. Leave empty when not known.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: The six digit PIN code the customer gave, digits only. Leave empty when not known.

response_fields.valid: false when the PIN code is not valid or nothing was given.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: valid={{ valid | default('') }}, route={{ route | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The service area check did not answer. Carry on without it; the service system routes the request from the city and PIN code.

tools.name: find_products
tools.description: Searches the Tiffany Designs product catalogue. Use it when the customer wants to buy something or asks what a product costs, and to get the product codes place_order needs. An empty query lists everything. Only products it returns may be named. The answer has a message with each product's name, product code (for place_order, never read out) and list price in rupees, and the field found.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The product the customer described, in English, for example study table, wardrobe or kids bed. Leave empty to list every product.

response_fields.products: Each product with name, product_code (for place_order, never read out) and price in rupees.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: found={{ found | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The product list did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:find_products once more. When it fails again, say the product list is not available right now and offer a call back from the sales team.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Saves a new order for the sales team, who call the customer to confirm the final price, delivery and payment. No payment is taken. Confirm the products, quantities, name, mobile number and delivery address with the customer before calling. The answer has a message with the order number and total list price to give, or what is missing, and the fields created, spoken_order_number (say it digit by digit) and total (list price in rupees).

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's full name as they gave it.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit mobile number, as confirmed with the customer: customer_phone when the customer agreed to use it, otherwise the number the customer gave.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Every product and quantity the customer confirmed, as product code x quantity separated by commas, using the product codes from find_products, for example TD-STD-01 x 1, TD-CHR-01 x 2.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House or flat number, street and area of the delivery address.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City of the delivery address.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Indian state of the delivery address, for example Haryana.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code of the delivery address.

parameters.name: notes
parameters.description: Anything else the customer asked the sales team to know, such as a preferred delivery time, in one short English sentence. Leave empty when there is nothing.

response_fields.created: true when the order is saved.
response_fields.order_id: Salesforce record id; not sent to the agent.
response_fields.spoken_order_number: The order number to say, digit by digit.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: created={{ created | default('') }}, spoken_order_number={{ spoken_order_number | default('') }}, total={{ total | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The order could not be saved because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:place_order once more with the same details. When it fails again, call tool:request_human_callback with the confirmed products, their quantities and the delivery city.

tools.name: save_customer_details
tools.description: Saves a new customer's details: name, mobile number, email, another phone number and address. For a customer already on record nothing is overwritten; the details go to the service team to confirm with the customer first. Confirm the details with the customer before calling. The answer has a message saying what happened, or what is missing, and the fields saved and new_customer (true when a new customer was created, false when the change went to the team).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The customer's 10 digit mobile number: customer_phone when it is set, otherwise the number the customer gave and confirmed.

parameters.name: customer_name
parameters.description: The customer's full name. Needed for a new customer.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The customer's email address, written without spaces, for example ravi.kumar@gmail.com. Leave empty when not given.

parameters.name: alternate_phone
parameters.description: Another phone number the customer gave, 10 digits. Leave empty when not given.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: House or flat number, street and area. Leave empty when not given.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City of the address. Leave empty when not given.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Indian state of the address, for example Haryana. Leave empty when not given.

parameters.name: postal_code
parameters.description: Six digit PIN code of the address. Leave empty when not given.

response_fields.new_customer: true when a new customer was created; false when the change went to the team to check.

tools.resp_template:
{{ message }}
Fields: saved={{ saved | default('') }}, new_customer={{ new_customer | default('') }}{% if error is defined %}, error={{ error }}{% endif %}
tools.on_failure: The details could not be saved because the service system did not answer. Apologise briefly and call tool:save_customer_details once more. When it fails again, tell the customer the details are noted for the service team, who will update them.
